raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44097
* #39294 (merged)

CI is run only on the top PR, #44097, which contains both changes.

#39294 was squash-merged as `ee30dc4d40993045273f0a90260db7efa302c214`. This PR is now based directly on main and contains only the compaction commits.

Current head: `683cf507a5e16833fe815ec5691405b0e62b4ea7`.

## Motivation

Unified Mamba/Conv compaction uses a gathered state tensor when relocating slots, which can OOM precisely when the allocator is reclaiming memory.

Seokwoo Song's four compaction commits are preserved, rebased onto main after #39294 was squash-merged.

## Modifications

- Copy disjoint physical state envelopes directly with the existing `copy_pages` kernel, removing the main-state gather temporary.
- Preserve main's `move_physical_pages` entry point, which calls the optimized move implementation.
- Retain sibling-state copying and ordinary copy-on-write behavior.
- Cover Mamba and Conv-only pools, both growth directions, eager/urgent/opportunistic compaction, state payloads and mappings, CUDA stream ordering, and CUDA graph readback.

## Accuracy Tests

Pre-merge validation base: `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`. Both PRs replayed without conflicts, and all eight patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`. The exact combined top commit passed **87 tests / 211 subtests** on H200 (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130), covering dLLM KV reuse, prefill budget, joint reclaim, SWA page estimation, Mamba/Conv compaction and views (CPU and CUDA), and adjacent HiCache ordering/regressions. All changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Earlier CI follow-up, before this main rebase: reproduced the `get_extend_allocation_demand` failure in `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` before the correction. After updating the fake allocator in #39294, **66 tests / 162 subtests passed** across the dLLM KV-reuse, prefill-budget, joint-eviction, tri-pool reclaim, and SWA paged-extend suites on the H200 host (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130). All six dLLM tests passed. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

The latest main rebase and restack preserve all four reclaim patches and all four compaction patches unchanged (`git range-diff`). The dLLM test-allocator interface correction remains included in #39294.

Earlier validation on B300 before this main rebase, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.14.1+cu130:

- Focused compaction/views suite: **12 tests / 47 subtests passed**, with CPU and CUDA cases actually executed.
- Adjacent state-transfer, pending-event, tri-pool, page-layout, and byte-accounting suite: **114 tests / 787 subtests passed**.
- Both this fix and the reclaim fix from #39294 in a separate combined snapshot: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**.
- All **18 CUDA scratch-bound configurations** fail against unchanged main production code and pass with this change: 12 Mamba configurations and 6 Conv-only configurations.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Review verified the physical-slot/page contract, disjoint move sources/destinations, current-stream execution, envelope layout and sink handling, sibling payload copying, and ordinary COW behavior. The pending-reader test injects the pending-reuse state after a real copy and validates the CUDA drain/reuse boundary; it does not claim end-to-end reproduction of that routing race.

The CPU fallback and sibling callbacks retain their own scratch-allocation behavior. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU validation is claimed. Historical serving/performance evidence is retained below and is not validation of this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh regression tests validate the reduced allocation peak and preserved payloads. No new latency or serving-throughput claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add and validate regression tests.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [ ] Documentation: not applicable; no new user-facing API or configuration.
- [ ] Fresh model accuracy / serving performance benchmarks: not run for this rebase.

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Unified compaction can OOM while reclaiming capacity because `MambaPool.copy_from` gathers selected states into a temporary GPU tensor. This affects both Mamba state and Conv-only state in FULL/SWA/Conv tri-pools: Conv-only models also use `UnifiedMambaPool`.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Copy disjoint physical state slots directly with the existing `copy_pages` kernel. FULL/SWA already use this path. Ordinary COW, sibling callbacks and allocator synchronization remain unchanged.
- Test Mamba and Conv-only compaction, payload/mapping preservation, graph readback and asynchronous ordering. New real-factory tri-pool tests cover CPU/CUDA, page sizes 1/4, eager/urgent/opportunistic moves, and live SWA relocation after Conv reclamation.
- Remove main-state gather scratch; sibling callbacks and the CPU fallback may still allocate scratch.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Base `27b68303d043`; head `c01a063a6325`. RTX 5090, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, TP=1. Qwen results are from `fce2d590f514`; the new commit changes tests only.

- **Regression:** Mamba 5 tests; Conv-only 2 tests / 12 configurations; related tests 54 / 127 subtests passed. Baseline fails all 6 Conv CUDA scratch checks. Offline cold-cache tests and all-files pre-commit passed.
- **Controlled OOM:** baseline fails 120 MiB temporal and 16 MiB Conv allocation requests. Each patched case moves **120 states** correctly with **5,120 bytes** extra allocated peak.
- **Output consistency:** Qwen3.5-4B and Inkling each pass **1,152 same-process comparisons** of token IDs/logprobs/top-5. Separate runs: Qwen **192/192** exact; Inkling **192/192 token sequences**, **191/192 logprob/top-5 records** exact. The Inkling discrepancy also occurs in baseline repetition; its cause is unresolved. Conv byte audits report zero mismatches.

Inkling uses a reduced checkpoint, fixed valid token IDs, graphs disabled and a shared SM120 GEMM override; this is output consistency, not task accuracy or stock-runtime certification. Qwen graphs are enabled. Prior Qwen cross-harness variability, incomplete original shutdown/pending-event evidence and shared HiCache failures remain disclosed in the evidence. Full HiCache and multi-GPU validation are not claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

96 requests per arm, outputs 32/64/128/192 tokens; startup, warmup and shutdown excluded. Paired geometric throughput changes, bootstrap 95% CIs:

| Comparison | Change | 95% CI |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B, 6 independent pairs | +3.09% | −1.39% to +8.13% |
| Inkling, 12 independent pairs | **−1.38%** | −3.01% to +0.18% |
| Inkling, 4 warmed pairs in one worker, no move instrumentation | **+0.04%** | -0.74% to +0.86% |

Original Inkling tails: 32-token E2E p95 **+3.74%**, 192-token TTFT p95 **+6.26%**. The earlier instrumented diagnostic measured throughput −1.09%. The new warmed comparison gives **+1.05% / +1.51%** for those two tails, with **384/384 output sequences exact**. It does not replace the independent runs or establish their cause; no uniform latency bound or serving speedup is claimed.

**Profiling the original p95-contributing requests:** Conv copy uses **1 kernel / 1.76–2.16 μs**, versus **12 kernels / 37.96–39.69 μs**, with no added synchronization. Copies occur after those requests' measured TTFT/32-token completion. Copy microbenchmarks show **74–84% lower wall time** and **zero main-state scratch** (baseline 36 KiB per moved Inkling state). Detailed traces, raw runs and limitations are retained separately.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Documentation: not applicable; this internal compaction fix introduces no user-facing API or configuration. The source comment explains the scope of scratch allocation removal. Accuracy validation above compares outputs; no task-benchmark accuracy score is claimed.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -1135,9 +1135,21 @@ def __init__(
     # take PHYSICAL slot ids; callers translate via the slot allocator first.
 
     def move_kv_cache(self, tgt_loc: torch.Tensor, src_loc: torch.Tensor):
-        # Ids are PHYSICAL slots; `MambaPool.copy_from` takes (src, dst), hence
